usage: fleet-switchboard notice [-h] [--from SENDER]
                                {pr,withdraw,ack} pr [note ...]

`notice pr` records a heads-up about a PR for the person's Decisions panel:
information, not a decision. It sends no message and wakes nobody. Send it as
soon as you OPEN the PR, so it is seen while CI and review run. It stays until
the PR is merged or closed; sending it again refreshes the note. A number that
is not an OPEN pull request is refused when you send it (an unreadable lookup
never blocks). `notice withdraw <pr>` removes a notice (the agent that sent
it, or its boss); a notice whose PR cannot be read for an hour is dropped.

positional arguments:
  {pr,withdraw,ack}  `pr` records a notice; `withdraw` removes the one for a
                     PR (its sender or its boss); `ack` (you, in a plain
                     shell) drops an order heads-up by its id
  pr                 The pull request: owner/repo#N or its URL (an issue, a
                     number that is not an open PR, is refused)
  note               Optional: one line of why, or what you intend (at most
                     300 characters)

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --from SENDER      Lab only: the sender's fleet name

usage: fleet-switchboard merge-gate [-h] [--pass | --check | --release]
                                    [--rerun-held] [--json]
                                    pr

Prints ONE block: the branch tip now, the branch tip the pull request's last
CI run was computed on, equal or not, the run's result at the current head,
the latest completed run on the branch and whether a merge is allowed now and
why. It writes nothing. `--pass` re-runs that pull request's CI on the current
merge ref when the branch moved (a close and reopen: head and labels
untouched; a held pull request only with `--rerun-held`), waits up to
`merge_gate.wait_minutes` (default 45), and on green records the pass and
takes the lock of the repository and branch. `--check` (the shim) exits 0 to
allow and 10 to refuse.

positional arguments:
  pr            The pull request: owner/repo#N or its URL

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit
  --pass        Run the gate, re-run CI if the branch moved, take the lock and
                record the pass
  --check       What the gh shim asks: exit 0 allow, 10 refuse (one line on
                stderr)
  --release     Release the lock you hold on the pull request's branch
  --rerun-held  With --pass: close and reopen a HELD pull request to recompute
                its merge ref (its orchestrator agrees first)
  --json

usage: fleet-switchboard orders [-h] [--cos] {list,add,copy,remove} ...

The owner's standing orders live in the charter issue's `## Standing orders`
section on GitHub, one per bullet: `- <text> (ordered by <name>, <YYYY-MM-
DD>)`. The switchboard re-supplies them to every agent of the charter at its
start, after each compaction and when they change, and the policy judge reads
them at every tool call. `list` is open to anyone. `add` and `remove` are for
the chief-of-staff only (you are identified by your pane); they edit only that
section of the issue body. `--cos` prints the Chief of Staff's OWN standing
orders: one local markdown file the owner edits (nothing here writes it).

positional arguments:
  {list,add,copy,remove}
    list                The charter's standing orders, numbered
    add                 Chief of Staff only: record one standing order the
                        owner gave
    copy                Chief of Staff only: copy every order of a sibling
                        charter to this one, wording and dates unchanged
    remove              Chief of Staff only: remove one order the owner
                        revoked

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --cos                 PR 18: print the Chief of Staff's own standing orders
                        file and its path (read-only: the owner edits that
                        file in an editor; there is no write command)

    template            Print a prefilled plan for an ask: its Done-when
                        clauses and one scenario stub per clause (read-only)
    review              The plan review engine (off unless
                        plan_review.enabled): adversarial lanes, at most 3
                        rounds

usage: fleet-switchboard pr-explain [-h] [--before BEFORE] [--after AFTER]
                                    [--body-file BODY_FILE] [--check]
                                    pr

Reads the PR once and PRINTS the block for its description; it writes nothing.
Paste it, or use --body-file to get the whole new body with the block in once,
then `gh pr edit --body-file`. --check judges the description the PR has.

positional arguments:
  pr                    The pull request: owner/repo#N or its URL

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --before BEFORE       The behaviour before, one or two lines
  --after AFTER         The behaviour after, one or two lines
  --body-file BODY_FILE
                        A file with a PR body (or - for the PR's own): print
                        it with the block in once
  --check               Judge the PR description: one block, a real why part,
                        no generated summary flowchart

usage: fleet-switchboard pr-state [-h] [--json] pr

Reads the daemon's cached picture of the PR (pr-state.json) and the local
ledger, and prints one line. It never calls GitHub: a PR the daemon has not
cached is 'unknown'. Use it instead of polling GitHub in a shell loop; wait
with `remind`.

positional arguments:
  pr          The pull request: owner/repo#N or its URL

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --json      The same, as one JSON object

usage: fleet-switchboard preflight-pr [-h]

Runs, each under the `heavy` wrapper and a time ceiling: the command-surface
snapshot class, the hygiene and role-file classes, bin/check-public-names and,
when files under cloud/ changed against the base, the cloud suites with TMPDIR
a 49-character token-shaped directory name. Only runs tests: it never pushes,
labels or records a verdict.

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

usage: fleet-switchboard plan review [-h]
                                     {start,verdict,respond,status,abandon,decide,close,report,tick} ...

positional arguments:
  {start,verdict,respond,status,abandon,decide,close,report,tick}
    start               Open a review of a plan for its ask and launch the
                        lanes
    verdict             (fallback) a lane records its verdict block for its
                        own lane
    respond             The planner answers a finished round: response table
                        and the new revision
    status              Rounds, lanes, open objections and the tally
    abandon             Clear a stalled open review (the round count
                        continues)
    decide              Resolve an escalated objection: accept it, or override
                        it with a reason
    close               The closing round: every lane confirms the final
                        revision, then the consensus is recorded
    report              What the review cost and what the reviewers caught
    tick                Housekeeping: relaunch a stuck lane once, then
                        escalate it; remind an undecided escalation

  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
